correctness.rationale: The grounding and strict positive Hessian give a unique connected optimal budget allocation. Tree Cauchy–Schwarz yields the reference weights. Exact chord voltage response identifies Q_n and KKT with a feasible improving perturbation proves both price branches, including equality. Covariance proves strict nested thresholds. Uniform singular quadrature gives the arcsine limit; an exact weighted double sum with a square-root Euler power sum, integrable endpoint-regularized trapezoid errors and weighted O(log n) remainders yields the \(2\pi\zeta(-1/2)\sqrt n\) correction. Replayed standalone finite checks: 4793 assertions, including linear algebra, numerical derivatives, nesting, continuum and residual bounds. Finite checks are not used as the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The indexed price boundary has direct economic meaning for when a budget-optimal network should reject a chord. Strict endpoint nesting gives a structural ordering; the continuum arcsine kernel permits macroscopic location-dependent pricing, while the negative \(2\pi\zeta(-1/2)\sqrt n\) correction quantifies discrete finite-size design at a previously unresolved scale. This structural result is not merely a finite numerical optimization or a trivial instance of convexity.
